result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [IPCRidge]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | greenwood description: IPC-weighted ridge regression for survival data. twitter-card: title: >- [IPCRidge]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | greenwood description: IPC-weighted ridge regression for survival data. title: "[IPCRidge]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: IPC-weighted ridge regression for survival data. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} IPC-weighted ridge regression for survival data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L250-L479){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature IPCRidge( alpha=1.0, *, standardize=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A linear survival model that corrects for censoring bias via inverse-probability-of-censoring (IPC) reweighting rather than the Cox partial likelihood. The model fits a weighted ridge regression on observed (uncensored) log-times: $$ \hat{\beta} = \arg\min_{\beta} \sum_{i:\,\delta_i=1} w_i \bigl(\log T_i - X_i \beta\bigr)^2 + \alpha \|\beta\|_2^2 $$ where $w_i = 1 / \hat{G}(T_i^-)$ are IPC weights from the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the censoring distribution. This eliminates censoring bias from the least-squares objective without assuming proportional hazards. Centering and optional standardization are applied before fitting, and coefficients are returned on the original covariate scale. The intercept is always estimated. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Ridge penalty strength. `0` gives unpenalized IPC-weighted OLS. [standardize]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Standardize covariates to unit variance before penalizing (default `True`). Coefficients are returned on the original scale. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit an IPC-weighted ridge on the lung dataset: ::: {#8ea84921 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") ridge = gw.IPCRidge(alpha=1.0).fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) ridge ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` IPCRidge (IPC-weighted ridge, alpha=1.0) coef (Intercept) 6.107 age -0.02134 sex 0.573 n = 228, events = 165 (used for fitting) ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [fit()](#fit){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Fit the IPC-weighted ridge regression to survival data. | | [predict()](#predict){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Predict from the fitted IPC-weighted ridge model. | | [to_frame()](#to_frame){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Return the coefficient table as a DataFrame. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the IPC-weighted ridge regression to survival data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L322-L421){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature fit( surv, covariates=None, *, data=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Only uncensored subjects contribute to the fit. Each is weighted by $1/\hat{G}(T_i^-)$ from the Kaplan-Meier censoring estimate, so subjects who experienced events when censoring was heavy receive greater influence. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response, built with `gw.Surv(time=..., event=...)`. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side sets `covariates`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe (pandas or polars), a 2-D array, or a formula string (e.g., `"age + sex"`) evaluated against `data`. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `covariates`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [IPCRidge]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator with cached coefficient arrays. ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict from the fitted IPC-weighted ridge model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L423-L458){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature predict( newdata=None, *, type="lp", ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariate values for prediction. `None` uses the training data. A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["lp"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Prediction type: - `"lp"`: the linear predictor $\hat{\beta}_0 + X\hat{\beta}$ (predicted log-time). Higher values indicate longer expected survival. - `"response"`: $\exp(\text{lp})$, predicted survival time on the original scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Predicted values, shape `(n_subjects,)`. ::: ### [to_frame()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the coefficient table as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L466-L479){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature to_frame( *, format=None, ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns: `term`, `estimate`. :::
